title: A City Under the Waves: Why Coral Reefs Matter to Everyone
title_zh: 浪下的城市：珊瑚礁为何与每个人有关
intro_zh: 本文约 576 词，围绕珊瑚礁的生态、经济、护岸、药物与气候价值展开，语言难度适合 CET-4，重点词约 6 个。

paragraphs.en: When people hear the word 'coral,' they often picture a bright decoration in a fish tank. In fact, a coral reef is closer to a busy city under the sea. It is built by tiny animals, and it gives food and shelter to thousands of ocean creatures. Though reefs cover less than 1 percent of the sea floor, they support about 25 percent of all marine species. That number alone makes them a global treasure.
paragraphs.zh: 人们听到“珊瑚”这个词时，常常会想到鱼缸里鲜艳的装饰。其实，珊瑚礁更像海底一座繁忙的城市。它由微小的动物建造，为成千上万的海洋生物提供食物和栖身之处。尽管珊瑚礁只覆盖不到1%的海底，却支撑着约25%的海洋物种。仅这个数字就足以说明它是全球珍宝。

paragraphs.en: Reefs are not just beautiful. They provide natural services that humans receive every day. Fish that live around reefs feed millions of people, especially in island countries. Reefs also act as nurseries for young fish. When these fish grow up, they swim out to the open ocean and later become food or income for fishing families. A healthy reef can keep a fishing community working for years.
paragraphs.zh: 珊瑚礁不只是美丽。它们提供人类每天都受益的自然服务。生活在珊瑚礁周围的鱼养育着数百万人，尤其是在岛国。珊瑚礁还是幼鱼的育婴场。这些鱼长大后游向开阔大洋，后来成为渔民家庭的食物或收入。健康的珊瑚礁能让一个渔业社区多年有生计。

paragraphs.en: Reefs also protect coastlines. Their hard structures slow down waves before the waves reach the shore. In some places, a reef can reduce wave energy by as much as 97 percent. That means less flooding and less damage during storms. For many low-lying islands, a reef is a natural sea wall. Building a concrete wall instead would cost a great deal of money and could harm the environment.
paragraphs.zh: 珊瑚礁也保护海岸线。它们坚硬的构造在波浪到达岸边之前削弱海浪。在某些地方，珊瑚礁能把海浪能量减少多达97%。这意味着风暴期间洪水更少、破坏更小。对许多低洼岛屿来说，珊瑚礁是一道天然海堤。若改用混凝土墙，不仅花费巨大，还可能损害环境。

paragraphs.en: The economic value is large, too. Reef-related tourism brings visitors who dive, snorkel, and stay in local hotels. In Australia, the Great Barrier Reef supports thousands of jobs and adds billions of dollars to the economy. In smaller countries, even a modest reef can be a main source of income. Travelers come to see fish, sea turtles, and soft corals moving with the water.
paragraphs.zh: 经济价值也很大。与珊瑚礁相关的旅游业带来潜水、浮潜和入住当地酒店的游客。在澳大利亚，大堡礁支撑着数千个工作岗位，并为经济增加数十亿美元。在较小的国家，即使一片不大的珊瑚礁也可能成为主要收入来源。游客前来观看鱼儿、海龟，以及随水摆动的软珊瑚。

paragraphs.en: There is another reason to care: medicine. Many reef animals produce chemicals to defend themselves or to communicate. Scientists study these chemicals and have developed drugs from them. A sea sponge, for example, helped lead to a medicine for a serious viral disease. Reefs may hold more surprises, but we will lose them if reefs disappear.
paragraphs.zh: 还有一个关心的理由：药物。许多礁区动物会制造化学物质来自卫或交流。科学家研究这些化学物质，并从中开发出药物。例如，一种海绵帮助促成了一款治疗严重病毒性疾病的药物。珊瑚礁可能还藏着更多惊喜，但如果珊瑚礁消失，我们就会失去它们。

paragraphs.en: Reefs are also part of the climate story. The ocean absorbs much of the extra heat trapped by greenhouse gases. Coral animals are sensitive to temperature. When the water becomes too warm for too long, they lose the tiny algae that live inside them and give them color and food. This is called coral bleaching. A bleached reef is not dead at once, but it is weak and may not survive if the heat continues.
paragraphs.zh: 珊瑚礁也是气候故事的一部分。海洋吸收了温室气体困住的额外热量中的很大一部分。珊瑚动物对温度很敏感。当海水变得过热且持续时间过长时，它们会失去生活在体内、赋予它们颜色和食物的微小藻类。这被称为珊瑚白化。白化的珊瑚礁不会立刻死亡，但它很虚弱；如果高温持续，它可能无法存活。

paragraphs.en: Human pressure adds to the problem. Pollution from farms and cities can flow into the sea and block sunlight. Heavy boats can break coral branches. Careless divers can touch or stand on reefs. But there is good news: reefs can recover when the pressure is removed. Protected areas, better waste systems, and careful tourism give corals time to grow again. Some groups also plant young corals in damaged areas.
paragraphs.zh: 人类压力加剧了问题。来自农场和城市的污染会流入大海并遮挡阳光。沉重的船只可能撞断珊瑚枝。粗心的潜水者可能触碰或踩踏珊瑚礁。但有好消息：当压力被消除时，珊瑚礁可以恢复。保护区、更好的废物处理系统和谨慎的旅游会给珊瑚重新生长的时间。一些团体还在受损区域种植幼珊瑚。

paragraphs.en: Protecting reefs is not only a job for scientists. Visitors can choose tours that do not touch corals. Families can use fewer chemicals that may reach the sea. Students can learn about local reefs and share what they find. Small actions, repeated by many people, can make a difference.
paragraphs.zh: 保护珊瑚礁不只是科学家的工作。游客可以选择不触碰珊瑚的旅游项目。家庭可以使用更少可能流入大海的化学用品。学生可以了解当地的珊瑚礁，并分享自己的发现。许多人都重复做的小行动，能够带来改变。

paragraphs.en: A coral reef looks quiet from a boat, but under the water it is full of life. It feeds us, guards our coasts, and opens a door to new medicines. It is also fragile. If we want that underwater city to remain, we must treat it as a shared home, not as a pretty background.
paragraphs.zh: 从船上望去，珊瑚礁很安静，但在水下它充满生命。它养育我们，守护我们的海岸，还打开通往新药物的大门。它也很脆弱。如果我们想让那座海底城市继续存在，就必须把它当作共同的家园，而不是漂亮的背景。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How coral reefs are built by tiny animals.
Why coral reefs are valuable and need protection.
How to build concrete sea walls on islands.
Why tourists enjoy diving in Australia.
questions.explain: 主旨题。全文从生态、经济、海岸保护、药物和气候等角度说明珊瑚礁的重要价值，并呼吁保护，因此B最全面。

questions.q: According to the passage, how much of the sea floor do coral reefs cover?
questions.explain: 细节题。第一段明确说 reefs cover less than 1 percent of the sea floor，25 percent 指的是海洋物种比例。

questions.q: What can be inferred about a bleached reef?
options: It is always dead at once.
It may recover if the heat stops.
It grows faster in warm water.
It is caused mainly by too many fish.
questions.explain: 推断题。第六段说白化的珊瑚礁不会立刻死亡，但很虚弱；如果高温持续可能无法存活，由此可推知条件改善时仍可能恢复。

questions.q: In the last paragraph, the word 'fragile' is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 词义题。fragile 意为“脆弱的、易受伤害的”，与 easily harmed 最接近；其他选项与上下文不符。
